//: This corpus is `corpus_ts` plus this file, and nothing else: all 29 sources are byte-identical
copies, which tests/test_bench_corpus_typed.py asserts on every run. It isolates one variable.
WHY IT EXISTS. `corpus_ts` reports both LSP arms as unanswered, and bench/README.md explains that
by its missing tsconfig: without a project file `tsserver` treats every file as its own inferred
project, cannot see across files, and returns an empty reference list. This tree tests that.
WHAT IT FOUND. Two blockers, in series. The tsconfig is one. The other was in this repository:
`providers/lsp.py`'s `_split_target_file_hint` returned early on any target without an `@file`
hint, so `StrategyChain.resolve` reached Serena verbatim while Serena name paths are
slash-separated, and references were never requested. With that fixed, this tree scores the
class-qualified pair at 100% on both LSP arms; `corpus_ts`, lacking only this file, still reports
Deliberately minimal: no `paths`, no `baseUrl`. Every import in the corpus is relative, and an
alias map would change how the ORACLE resolves specifiers, a second variable.
